doc.title: Doug Carn interviewed by Monk Rowe, via Zoom, February 24, 2023

title: The Jazz Is Dead label and claims that jazz is dead
summary: Carn recounts being tricked into the Jazz Is Dead label name and says jazz has been declared dead since fusion.

story.theme_name: Where jazz stands today: young players, rock, and the audience
story.community_name: How the music business changed: hype, youth and lost apprenticeship

blocks.x: Well thanks for sharing that. I’d like to — before we’re done here I want to just ask you about the last few years. It’s been interesting because some of your music from the 70s has been revisited and now they’re calling it classic, and at the same time you got hooked up with the two fellas from the Jazz Is Dead label and I just find it an interesting pairing.

Well that’s the biggest trick that’s been played on me in my life. They said, “Look, man, we’ve got some hip-hop tracks and we want to dub you on a couple of them. Gary Bartz is going to do some and Roy Ayers is going to do some.” I said, “Okay, how much you going to pay me?” So we agreed on a price but they didn’t say the name on the label is going to be Jazz Is Dead, and be promoting a concept named Jazz Is Dead. They didn’t’ say nothing about that. I didn’t know nothing about that until it came out. And when I say

“tricked me” I don’t mean a dirty stab in the back trick you know, they just didn’t say nothing about it you know. And that didn’t rattle me too much you know, but we played a gig and we’d go in the auditorium and all these Jazz Is Dead posters was all over the walls and it was kind of discouraging you know, but they’re intelligent young men, they’re clean cut and I give them a break. But I tell any young people, older people too, if you’re going to tear something down and destroy it, make sure you’ve got something to replace it with.
Good point. It’s interesting that they didn’t tell you about that because it seems like it was a calculated move.

It was calculated, and a lot of my jazz fans, it hurt them you know, and they thought that I had sold out you know. I said, “Well if I sold out, I sold out for free because I ain’t got no money.” You know? But they’ve been saying jazz is dead a long time you know, just like they say God is dead you know, ever since fusion came in you know.
Yeah every couple of years you see it in the jazz magazines and I think it’s just like okay it’s time to write about that again, because it’s just something to write about.

Right. Because in the 70s the fusion started, they were saying jazz is dead. But then here comes Wynton Marsalis you know, playing more jazz than anybody ever played you know, and all these young people and jazz programs in colleges and universities. You know that’s the thing about America and a free society. It’s free speech you know, and people can say what they want to say, can believe what they want to be and you can’t get bent out of shape. You know if jazz is dead then classical music has got to be dead a long time. But Beethoven, Bach and Brahms, they’re just as big as they ever were you know. Especially in Europe.
